# Git Light — Full site content

> Git Light is a free, MIT-licensed desktop Git client for macOS, Windows, and Linux with a graph-first interface — commit graph, branch sidebar, working tree, multi-repo tabs, and real local Git operations via the native Git CLI. No account or subscription required.

Version: 1.3.0 · License: MIT · Author: ftuyama · Stack: Tauri 2, Vue 3, TypeScript, Rust, Pinia, Tailwind CSS 4

Website: https://ftuyama.github.io/git-light/ (also in Brazilian Portuguese: https://ftuyama.github.io/git-light/pt-BR/, Spanish: https://ftuyama.github.io/git-light/es/, French: https://ftuyama.github.io/git-light/fr/, German: https://ftuyama.github.io/git-light/de/, Simplified Chinese: https://ftuyama.github.io/git-light/zh-CN/ and Japanese: https://ftuyama.github.io/git-light/ja/)
Repository: https://github.com/ftuyama/git-light
Download: https://github.com/ftuyama/git-light/releases

---

## Overview

Git Light is a desktop Git client with a graph-first interface. It provides a three-pane repository view that runs real Git commands against local repositories via typed Tauri commands. Open a folder, clone from a URL, start a repo with init, browse history, manage branches, stage files, commit, fetch/pull/push, and inspect diffs.

Git Light is a Tauri 2 app. The renderer never shells out to Git directly — the Rust backend runs the native `git` CLI and exposes typed commands to the Vue 3 renderer.

## Features

### Clone, init & discovery
Clone from a URL with progress and cancel, start a repo with init, or scan a folder to find nested repositories. Opening a subfolder resolves to the repo root. No account required.

### Commit graph
Virtualized SVG lanes with a pending-changes row, infinite scroll, and arrow-key selection across history.

### Branch sidebar
Favorites, remotes, tags, stashes, and worktrees — drag branches to merge or rebase.

### Working tree
Flat or tree file list, per-hunk staging, conflict resolution, and commit composition. File type icons per path.

### Diff viewer
Unified/split modes, syntax highlighting, per-hunk staging, blame overlay with file history, and word wrap. Binary images render side-by-side with zoom, pan, and a fullscreen lightbox.

### Interactive rebase
Reorder, squash, fixup, drop, or edit commits in a dialog before starting the rebase.

### Multi-repo tabs
Open several repositories at once — switch between tabs and pick up where you left off. Reopen the last closed tab, cycle with keyboard, or jump to a tab by index.

### Blame & file history
Inline blame overlay with author blocks, per-revision file history, and optional word wrap for long lines.

### Remote sync + auto-fetch
Fetch, pull, push, and sync from the toolbar — with ahead/behind counts in the status bar. Optional background auto-fetch on a configurable interval.

### Search & shortcuts
Search commits and files by message or path (non-matching graph rows dim). Navigate history and drive the UI from the keyboard — every shortcut is remappable in Settings → Shortcuts with conflict detection.

### Git output log
Per-tab drawer listing each executed git command with stdout/stderr and ok/error status. Clear per tab.

### Auto-update checks
Packaged builds compare against GitHub Releases on startup. Check manually anytime from the app menu.

### Real Git backend
Native `git` CLI in the Rust backend via typed Tauri commands — mock mode available for UI-only dev.

### Credits & attribution
Settings credits panel with project links and open-source licenses. Native About dialog on all platforms.

### System terminal
Open an embedded terminal docked under the commit graph at the repo root with ⌘J. Use the panel's external-link button for the OS terminal.

### Themes & UI mode
Default, Dracula, Light, Claude, Tokyo Night, Nord, Gruvbox, Rosé Pine, One Dark, Solarized Light, Custom, or System appearance. Custom lets you pick the base background, surface, text, accent, success, warning, and danger colors; the remaining tokens are derived. Basic mode hides advanced actions for a simpler toolbar.

### Polished layout
Collapsible sidebars with expand rails, resizable panes, and commit graph zoom for dense history views.

## Feature status matrix

| Area | Status |
|------|--------|
| Real Git backend (`git` CLI in Rust backend; renderer never shells out) | Supported |
| Open local repos · recent repos · multi-repo tabs (reopen closed, cycle, jump-to-index) · startup screen | Supported |

| Branch sidebar — favorites, tags, stashes, worktrees; drag-and-drop merge/rebase; section context menus | Supported |
| Working tree — flat/tree view, stage/unstage (patch hunks), commit, file type icons | Supported |
| Diff viewer — unified/split, syntax highlighting, per-hunk staging, blame overlay with file history, word wrap · image diffs (zoom, pan, lightbox) | Supported |
| Fetch / pull / push / sync · remote maintenance (fetch all, prune, push tags) · auto-fetch interval | Supported |
| Merge / rebase / interactive rebase / cherry-pick (continue/abort banner) | Supported |
| Merge conflict resolution (ours/theirs/per-block) | Supported |
| Undo / redo (reflog-backed) · stash · search | Supported |
| Git output log — per-tab executed commands with stdout/stderr | Supported |
| Command palette (⌘K) · customizable keyboard shortcuts (remappable, conflict detection) | Supported |
| Embedded terminal at the repo root (⌘J) + open in system terminal | Supported |
| Themes — Default, Dracula, Light, Claude, Tokyo Night, Nord, Gruvbox, Rosé Pine, One Dark, Solarized Light, Custom, System (settings) | Supported |
| Collapsible sidebars with expand rails · commit graph zoom | Supported |
| UI mode — Basic (essential actions) or Advanced (full toolbar and sidebar) | Supported |
| Open on GitHub · app preferences (appearance, layout, graph, sidebar, sync/auto-fetch, shortcuts, credits) | Supported |
| Credits & attribution (settings panel + native About dialog) | Supported |
| Resizable three-pane layout · file watcher auto-refresh | Supported |
| Auto-update check (packaged builds) · Check for Updates… menu | Supported |
| Clone (URL, progress + cancel) · init new repository · folder discovery | Supported |
| Hosting auth UI (OAuth sign-in, private-host browsing) | Not yet |

## Tech stack

Tauri 2, Vue 3, TypeScript, Rust, Pinia, reka-ui, Tailwind CSS 4, Vitest, Vite.

## Download & install

Download the latest installer from GitHub Releases:
- macOS: `.dmg` — open the DMG and drag Git Light to Applications
- Windows: `.exe` (NSIS) — run the installer
- Linux: `.AppImage` or `.deb`

Use **Git Light → Check for Updates…** to check for new versions in packaged builds.

### Build from source

```
git clone https://github.com/ftuyama/git-light.git
cd git-light
npm install
npm run dev
```

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Git Light really free?
Yes. MIT licensed, no paid tier, no trial, no ads, no feature gates. Every listed feature is available in the free build.

### Do I need a GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket account?
No. There is no sign-in, no license key and no telemetry. Git Light works with any repository on disk and with any remote your own Git is already configured for, over HTTPS or SSH.

### Does it work offline?
Yes. Browsing history, the commit graph, staging, diffs, commits, branches, merges, rebases and stashes are all local operations. Only fetch, pull, push and clone need network access.

### Does it come with its own Git install?
No. Git Light runs your system `git` binary, so your existing config, aliases, credential helper, SSH keys, hooks and `.gitignore` behaviour all apply unchanged.

### Can I use my existing repositories?
Yes. Open any folder that contains a `.git` directory, or clone or init a new one. Git Light adds no proprietary index and writes no extra files into your repository.

### Does it work on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs?
Apple Silicon (arm64) is fully supported. Intel Macs are not supported by the current builds, because the release pipeline only produces an `aarch64` `.dmg`. Windows x64 and Linux x86_64 builds are also available.

### macOS says the app is damaged or moves it to the Trash.
That is Gatekeeper reacting to an ad-hoc signature, not a broken download. Use the curl install script, or re-sign the app once with `codesign` and `xattr` as shown in the macOS install note.

### Which languages are supported?
English, Portuguese (Brazil) and Simplified Chinese. The UI follows your OS language and can be switched in Settings.
